faq.question: What is bacteriostatic water?
faq.answer: It is sterile water containing a bacteriostatic preservative, supplied as a laboratory diluent for reconstituting lyophilized research peptides. Exact composition is stated on the product label and COA.

faq.question: How does it differ from sterile water?
faq.answer: Bacteriostatic water contains a preservative that limits microbial growth, while sterile water (price-list code WA10) is unpreserved and intended for single-use laboratory preparation.

faq.question: Is it supplied with peptide orders?
faq.answer: Yes — diluent kits can be added to any peptide order; many buyers include one 10-vial diluent kit per peptide kit.

faq.question: Which kit sizes are available?
faq.answer: 10 mL × 10 vials (code BA10, US$8 per kit) and 3 mL × 10 vials (code BA3, US$7 per kit).
